For a flat fee of $49, AnswerTheComplaint provides a complete answer and/or counterclaim document with built-in rules and deadlines for all 50 states. It identifies potential FDCPA violations that may give the defendant grounds to countersue: calls before 8 AM or after 9 PM, threats of arrest, misrepresenting the debt amount, contacting third parties, and continuing contact after a cease-and-desist.

Filing an answer is the single most important step a person can take when sued for a debt. This service removes both the cost barrier and the knowledge barrier.

htmlContent:

Let me give you a preview of what August 29 looks like.

Rule 1: The Automatic Stay.
The moment you file for bankruptcy, every creditor must stop. Wage garnishment stops. Foreclosure stops. Repossession stops. Collection calls stop. Utility shutoffs stop. Pending lawsuits stop. It takes effect immediately upon filing. Most people do not know this exists until an attorney tells them, and most people cannot afford the attorney.

Rule 2: The 37 Day Rule.
Before a mortgage servicer can initiate a foreclosure sale, federal regulation requires them to wait at least 37 days after sending a pre-foreclosure notice. When a debt collector calls before 8 AM, threatens arrest, misrepresents what you owe, contacts your employer, or continues calling after you sent a written cease-and-desist, they have broken federal law. Those violations do not just make the harassment stop. They give you the legal basis to countersue.

These are three of the dozens of rules, protections, and strategies covered in the "Hold On, Don't Panic" seminar. Each one changes outcomes when people know about them.
